tagline: Correspondence chess with live updates over server-sent events
summary: A solid multiplayer core. Players can run many games at once, every change is pushed live over SSE, and move legality is decided on the server by chess.js, with each move stored as a row. There's chat, friends, challenges, presence, history navigation, captured pieces and synthesized sounds, plus a smoke test and a Docker setup. The README lists what's not done: real auth, clocks, ratings and takebacks. For a correspondence product, "your move" notifications and move deadlines matter most.

items: Multiple games in progress at once, shown as tiles with mini boards
Server-side legality, game-over detection and SAN from chess.js
Each move stored as a row, so history, captured pieces and threefold repetition come from replaying it
Click or drag to move, with legal-move hints
Move history navigation with buttons and arrow keys
Resign, and draw offer / accept / decline, with confirmation
Nickname sign-in that creates a player automatically
Mutual friends and nickname autocomplete
Challenges that wait for acceptance, plus instant new games
Online presence from open SSE connections
Live chat per game
One EventSource per tab, with targeted pushes (game, games, presence, friends, chat)
Heartbeat every 25 s, and automatic reconnect
Move and capture sounds synthesized with Web Audio
Docker Compose with MySQL and phpMyAdmin, plus a seed script
End-to-end smoke test against the real server and database
Email and password accounts with scrypt, and random session tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes
Default admin created on first boot, an admin page that lists and creates accounts, and admins can move for either side
reset-db and reset-password scripts. The seed script is removed
Profile moved into a narrow left sidebar. Empty game lists are hidden
Drag-only moves applied optimistically, rolled back if the server rejects them
Move and capture sounds from audio files instead of synthesized ones
Smoke test covers sign-in, the admin API and admin moves
More board.js and styles.css changes (36 insertions, 6 deletions)

nextSteps.title: Finish and merge accounts-admin-and-board-ux into main
nextSteps.why: Real auth and the admin page are already written. Until they're merged, main stays forgeable (the cookie holds the raw user id).

nextSteps.title: Email or Web Push notification when it's your move
nextSteps.why: The core feature of correspondence chess.

nextSteps.title: Days-per-move deadlines, with a timeout loss
nextSteps.why: Without them, abandoned games stay open forever.

nextSteps.title: PGN export from the moves table
nextSteps.why: Easy, since chess.js already produces SAN, and it opens games up to analysis tools.

nextSteps.title: Glicko-2 ratings and a leaderboard
nextSteps.why: Adds a reason to keep playing.

nextSteps.title: Stockfish WASM analysis board for finished games
nextSteps.why: Expected after a game, and runs in the browser with no server cost.

risks: main has nickname-only auth, so anyone can impersonate a player. The fix is on an unmerged branch
The SSE hub keeps state in memory, so more than one instance needs Redis or MySQL polling
There's one commit, so the history is coarse
phpMyAdmin is signed in automatically as root. Keep it out of any deployed compose file
